Frequently asked questions ChatGPT Sites lets you create, host, and share websites, apps, and games with ChatGPT. Start with an idea, refine it through conversation, and return anytime to make changes. No. Describe what you want in plain language and ChatGPT builds the Site with you. If you already have a compatible project, you can ask ChatGPT whether it can be published with Sites. Create dashboards, team trackers, client portals, landing pages, calculators, games, and more. Sites can also save progress and uploaded files so people can come back and continue their work. Sites is available during public beta with eligible ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, and Edu plans. Availability, usage limits ⁠ , and workspace controls vary by plan and region. See the Help Center ⁠ for current access and limits, or contact support ⁠ . New Sites start limited to you and workspace admins. Depending on your plan ⁠ and workspace settings ⁠ , you can invite selected people, share with your workspace, or make the Site public. External viewer invitations are rolling out on eligible plans ⁠ and may require approval. Yes. Owners can invite active members of the same workspace to edit. After the owner publishes the Site once, editors can make changes and publish updates. Editors can also access data saved in the Site. External viewers can’t edit. You can rename your ChatGPT-hosted URL or connect a custom domain you own. If you rename the hosted URL, the old address redirects to the new one. In eligible Business and Enterprise workspaces, people in the same workspace can choose to let a Site read information from supported tools they’ve connected to ChatGPT. The Site only sees what that person already has permission to access. It does not use the creator’s connections or make changes in those tools. Yes. Information from a visitor’s connected tools is only available while they’re using the Site and isn’t available to scheduled tasks running in the background.
